part.text: All tests pass. Let me also verify with the race detector since the tests are concurrency-heavy:

Done. Implemented the solution in `paasio.go` (no other files touched):

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`; `Read` delegates to the underlying reader, then atomically adds the byte count and increments the op count under a mutex. `ReadCount` returns the snapshot under the same mutex, so bytes and ops are always consistent even when read concurrently with `Read`.
- **`writeCounter`** — same design for `io.Writer` with `Write`/`WriteCount`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — embeds both counters to satisfy `ReadWriteCounter`, constructed by `NewReadWriteCounter` from an `io.ReadWriter`.

The single-mutex-per-counter design is what makes the consistency tests (`TestReadCountConsistency*`, `TestWriteCountConsistency*`) pass: since each read/write of 50 bytes updates `n` and `nops` together, any `ReadCount`/`WriteCount` snapshot always satisfies `nops == n / numBytes`.

Verification: `go test ./...` passes, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes as well.
